svg.title: Urban Analytics Lab lecture poster — 3 speakers

g.text: Rethinking cities in the age of AI

g.inkscape:label: Speaker 1
g.text: Dr. Yuan Lai, Associate Professor, Tsinghua University
The Street-Smart City: Using AI to Decode Urban Life from the Ground Up

text.tspan: True urban intelligence isn't just about sensors and speed; it's about understanding human
experiences. We present a "street-smart" AI framework that learns from the city's informal, ground-level
signals. By decoding the latent concerns in citizen service complaints, we reveal precise geographies of
public health risk. By reading street scenes through multimodal models, we quantify the potential for
social vitality beyond pedestrian counts. This work proposes a new form of urban science—where AI
translates everyday life into actionable knowledge for equitable health and design.

g.inkscape:label: Speaker 2
g.text: Dr. Steven Jige Quan, Associate Professor, Seoul National University
AI-aided Design for Participatory Urban Planning and Design

text.tspan: AI has increasingly shaped generative design through AI-aided design (AIAD). However, most work still
prioritizes supporting design experts over enabling meaningful public participation. This lecture defines
AIAD, situates it within major digital design models, and shows how emerging AIAD frameworks can
better empower participatory planning and design. Through illustrative examples, it highlights recent
advances enabled by GANs, Stable Diffusion, and large language models, and concludes with a
roadmap for integrating AIAD into participatory processes to advance sustainable city development.

g.inkscape:label: Speaker 3
g.text: Dr. Tan Yigitcanlar, Professor, Queensland University of Technology

text.tspan: This talk explores how advances in quantum computing could transform the way cities function and
are governed. Unlike conventional computers, quantum technologies can address highly complex
problems, creating new opportunities to improve everyday urban life. The presentation highlights
potential impacts on transport efficiency, climate and environmental forecasting, energy system
management, and infrastructure security. It also examines the implications for urban planning and
public decision making, emphasising the importance of governance, regulation, equity, and
institutional readiness as cities move toward a quantum-enabled future.

g.text: Hosts: Dr. Filip Biljecki, Dr. Shengxiao (Alex) Li
Talk 1 - The Street-Smart City: Using AI to Decode Urban Life from the Ground Up by Assoc Prof Yuan Lai
Talk 2 - AI-aided Design for Participatory Urban Planning and Design by Assoc Prof Steven Jige Quan
Talk 3 - Quantum Computing and the City by Prof Tan Yigitcanlar
Joint discussion session and Q/A moderated by Dr Shengxiao (Alex) Li
